assumptions: The concept remains at planning stage, so the cited reporting failures establish operational friction but not recurring demand or willingness to pay.

The initial buyer is a smaller Polish regulated financial entity with enough ICT-contract complexity to need more than the official spreadsheet and validation package, but without a capable enterprise GRC implementation already in place.

Production use would require a customer-controlled or tightly isolated deployment and qualified external support for regulatory interpretation; AI extraction would remain subordinate to provenance and human approval.
The founder can devote the stated 16-22 hours per week and use contractors without relying on employer time, data, vendors, or systems.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: The proposal correctly identifies a real gap between merely producing the public template and maintaining an approved, source-linked register across contracts, entities, and changing taxonomy rules. It also appropriately abandons generic form generation as the wedge. However, the observed rejection wave may largely reflect first-cycle learning, and the evidence does not establish that persistent lineage and remediation failures form a durable underserved need.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Rejected mandatory submissions and the need to reconcile contracts, providers, functions, and legal entities create credible compliance pain. Continued training indicates that accuracy remains salient. Yet the regulator supplies free materials and training, capable products already exist, and no evidence shows recurring failure frequency, budget ownership, paid demand, or savings large enough to support the proposed implementation and subscription charges.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Implementation revenue plus recurring licenses can support good economics if taxonomy logic, entity resolution, and approvals become reusable. The present wedge is nevertheless likely to be service-heavy, with costly security reviews, private deployments, expert interpretation, national-version maintenance, and long sales cycles. CAC, payback, retention, delivery hours, and achievable gross margin are all unknown, while the founder-wealth scenario depends on reaching 120 entities at pricing pressured by a public specialist alternative.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Smaller Polish financial entities with complex ICT estates and limited GRC engineering are a coherent initial segment, and SPR-PF-18 remediation provides a concrete trigger. The research does not quantify how many such entities lack adequate tools, suffer repeat failures, or have sufficient spend. Poland alone may be too narrow for the stated scale, while moving across the EU introduces regulator-specific workflows and localization costs.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Polish workflow specialization, clause-level lineage, and customer-controlled deployment could earn a useful niche. But the core standard and validation materials are public, ServiceNow already serves enterprise workflows, and a DORA-native specialist covers smaller buyers at disclosed prices. There is no exclusive distribution, proprietary access, regulatory privilege, or proven performance edge that presently supports a dominant position.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A trusted contract-to-register system could extend into other EU jurisdictions, continuous third-party risk governance, contract-change monitoring, vendor hierarchies, and adjacent regulatory evidence workflows. Those adjacencies reuse meaningful data and workflow primitives. Expansion is not frictionless, however, because each national submission process needs maintenance and the broader GRC market contains stronger incumbents.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Approved lineage, accumulated mappings, embedded review workflows, and a non-confidential remediation-pattern library could create moderate switching costs and gradual learning advantages. The regulatory schema is public, customer text cannot be pooled, exportability limits lock-in, and document extraction plus deterministic validation are reproducible by incumbents and focused entrants. The proposed compounding asset is plausible but weak until its learning rate and exclusivity are demonstrated.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: Source-clause provenance, human approvals, Polish submission fidelity, and private deployment could materially improve trust and remediation speed relative to a bare official template. No benchmark yet shows a decisive reduction in expert hours, rejection risk, or total cost, and existing vendors could add similar features. The offer is differentiated in design but not yet proven sufficiently better to change purchasing behavior.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: DORA implementation, documented 2025 rejections, continuing 2026 KNF education, and versioned reporting frameworks create a timely opening while operating practices are still forming. The same chronology is a risk: first-cycle errors may decline as teams learn, updated official tools may absorb the pain, and established vendors already have live offerings.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Boutique DORA advisors, auditors, MSPs, and banking-software consultancies are logical trust-bearing channels and suit the founder's low-publicity preferences. No partner has committed, advisors may prefer billable remediation or incumbent tools, and regulated entities may still subject the young vendor to direct security and procurement review. Repeatable CAC and sales-cycle evidence is absent.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The founder is well matched to structured-data validation, entity resolution, document AI, and a focused part-time pilot, and the stated initial capital appears adequate for validation. Production delivery adds financial-regulation interpretation, sensitive contract handling, security assurance, exact and continuously updated exports, liability control, and slow customer onboarding. Those requirements may exceed a part-time solo operation before demand is sufficient to support a team.

main_structural_strength: A mandatory, structured reporting workflow with documented validation failures aligns unusually well with the founder's data-validation skills, and the source-linked remediation wedge is more valuable than commodity form generation.
primary_score_limiter: There is no direct evidence that the target segment will pay this entrant enough to overcome free official substitutes, priced specialist competition, security procurement, and service-heavy delivery.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: The EBA and KNF provide the official data model, validation materials, current forms, examples, and free training, while both ServiceNow and a DORA-native vendor already offer register workflows and the specialist publishes annual pricing of EUR 1,500-12,500.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Paid pilots should demonstrate repeatable reductions in expert hours and validation failures, acceptance of the proposed security architecture, gross margin after onboarding and taxonomy maintenance, renewal intent, and at least one signed advisor channel commitment with measurable lead flow.
highest_value_structural_change: Make a trusted DORA advisor or managed-service provider the payer and prime contractor through a white-label, customer-controlled runtime priced per active entity or reporting cycle; let the partner retain remediation revenue while the product supplies lineage and deterministic validation, thereby reducing direct procurement friction and aligning rather than displacing the channel.
